Findings.Name: Server can write agent-trusted state
Findings.Detail: Write access reaches agent state (mcp-config, hooks, instructions), e.g. /Users/demo/.mcp.json, /Users/demo/.claude/settings.json, /Users/demo/CLAUDE.md. This repository's own .mcp.json or hooks are writable; a change would load new servers or run hooks the next time the repo is opened.
Findings.Fix: Scope this server to a directory that holds no MCP config, hooks, instruction, or memory files; keep those under version control so changes are visible.
Findings.Mapping: OWASP LLM06, MITRE ATLAS AML.T0051, CWE-732

attackPaths.name: Potential persistent agent compromise path
attackPaths.description: filesystem can write files the agent trusts in future sessions: /Users/demo/.mcp.json (mcp-config, runs code at next session start); /Users/demo/.claude/settings.json (hooks, runs code at next session start); /Users/demo/CLAUDE.md (instructions); and 3 more.
steps: browser brings external content into the agent's context
filesystem (file-write) modifies /Users/demo/.mcp.json (mcp-config, runs code at next session start)
next session loads the modified state and trusts it

evidence.detail: web content entering the browser enters the agent's context

attackPaths.impact: A modification made in one session would shape every later session. Because the writable state includes MCP configuration or hooks, a modification can start arbitrary code at the next session without any further instruction.
attackPaths.remediation: Scope filesystem to a directory that holds no agent configuration, instruction files, or hooks; keep a copy of those files under version control so changes are visible.

attackPaths.name: Potential sensitive data exfiltration path
attackPaths.description: filesystem can read project files, including any .env or key files in the tree and browser can send data to any network destination. Together they form a path an injected instruction could walk.
steps: instruction from a prompt, document, or tool result
filesystem (file-read) reads project files, including any .env or key files in the tree
browser (network-send) sends them to any network destination

evidence.detail: browser session can reach any destination

attackPaths.impact: An instruction the agent processes could combine these two capabilities to expose project files, including any .env or key files in the tree outside this machine. Nothing here proves it has happened; the path exists.
attackPaths.remediation: keep secrets out of the directories filesystem can read (use a secret manager rather than .env files); constrain browser to an allowlist of destinations. Either change alone removes the path.
